column1: # Known slow calls: our per-call cost against Metal's, where it is over an order of magnitude.
# READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A ROW. A row here is not an accepted difference and it is not permission
# for anything. It is a call that costs an order of magnitude more than Metal's over the cases both
# legs did exactly, written down so the one call that holds an open bug visible does not make every
# run red and teach everyone to stop reading the report. Nothing here is resolved by being listed.
# The gate is held in BOTH directions (src/slow_calls.rs): a call over the margin that is not
# listed fails the run, and a listed call that has come back inside the band fails it too, saying
# the row looks fixed and must go. So a row cannot outlive the bug it stands for.
# There is a third state, and it fails nothing: a row the measurement cannot resolve, or a whole
# measurement whose own instrument says it was taken on a CPU the figures cannot be compared across,
# is WITHHELD. Withholding neither adds a row nor retires one, and the run says which rows and why.
# Before adding a row, LOCALISE IT: `conformance times --runs 8 --call <name>` prints the call case
# by case. A per-call total says that a call is expensive and never where, and `replace_region` --
# the row this file was started for, and retired at the bottom of this header -- was 105x over the
# whole set and 1.2x over the three cases that obviously make it.
# AND THEN READ THE PER-CASE TOTAL BESIDE IT, WHICH IS THE CHECK THIS FILE WAS MISSING. Metal
# compiles the AIR at `MTLLibrary` creation and we translate it at pipeline creation and at
# reflection, so the same work sits at a DIFFERENT CALL on each leg -- README.md says so and says
# "neither row alone is a result", and five rows were nevertheless written here off the per-call
# figure alone. Measured over the stored 19:57 pass, per case, our leg against Metal's:
#   function-facts-*                 0.04x   (Metal 343 ms, ours 13 ms over 15 cases)
#   library-facts-descriptor-*       0.02x   (Metal 156 ms, ours 3.8 ms over 7)
#   function-bindings-*              0.15x   (Metal 320 ms, ours 49 ms over 13)
#   attribute-stride-*               0.07x
#   mesh-pipeline-reflection-*       0.43x
#   blend-sweep-*                    0.68x, with two cases at 1.25x and 1.55x
#   attribute-format-*               1.92x, with attribute-format-fetches at 2.68x
#   xr-two-plane*                    0.23x  -- and replace_region's row was a REAL bug, since fixed
# Metal pays 21-27 ms at `library` in every one of those cases and we pay 0.05-0.8 ms. So a call
# that reads 20x or 50x against Metal while its CASE reads 0.04x is not a cost finding at all; it
# is the placement of the compile, and a row that quotes only the per-call ratio tells a reader we
# are slow where we are 25 times faster.
# AND HERE IS WHAT THE PER-CASE FIGURES ACTUALLY SAY, which is the one finding in this cluster
# worth acting on. Sort every paired case by how many pipelines it creates on our leg:
#   pipelines a case creates    cases    median case ratio, ours over Metal
#   21 or more                    10     2.49x
# Metal compiles a library eagerly and we translate a variant when a pipeline needs it, so while a
# case makes few pipelines Metal's eager compile is largely wasted and we win by 4x to 14x. The
# advantage is spent by about twenty pipelines and REVERSES past that, because our per-pipeline
# cost stays where Metal's falls (and NOT because Metal's marginal pipeline is inherently cheap --
# the paragraph after the list says what it is). The ten cases past the turn, worst
# first: integer-vertex-attributes 3.62x (64 pipelines, Metal 37.8 ms against our 136.8 ms),
# vertex-format-constant-step 3.08x, attribute-format-fetches 2.68x, vertex-format-half4 2.60x,
# vertex-format-float4 2.52x, vertex-format-instance-step 2.46x, blend-sweep-write-masks 1.55x,
# blend-sweep-operations 1.25x, blend-interaction-mask-blend 1.05x, blend-sweep-operation-pairs
# WHY METAL'S MEDIAN FALLS, measured rather than inferred, and NOT an amortization. This file used
# to say Metal "amortizes 4.7x" across a case's pipelines (122.3 us median a call where a case makes
# one, 31.0 us at 5 to 15, 26.1 us at 36 or more, against ours at 1686.0, 1277.5 and 1205.6), which
# invites the reading that a marginal pipeline is cheap for Metal and dear for us, and so that
# something Metal does cheaply is being redone. It is not that.
# Metal's median falls because of what its cheap answers are, not because a marginal pipeline is
# cheap. Measured on Metal's own API with no Vulkan in the process
# (`probes/metal_pipeline_marginal_cost.m`), Metal has exactly three: an identical descriptor,
# memoised at 5-11 us; a change that reaches only a small stage, 45 us for a vertex format where a
# blend state over the same pair is 3.1 seconds; and an AIR that some earlier process compiled,
# since MTLCompilerService keys its output on the AIR and keeps it across processes -- 27 us warm
# against 4052 us cold. A distinct fragment-side state on a cold machine gets none of them and
# costs what compiling a new function costs (4052 us against 4783 us over a trivial fragment). So
# every figure in the 26.1 us column is one of those three answers, and the fall from 122.3 us is
# the mix of them, not a per-pipeline amortization a Vulkan driver could be failing to use.
# Both legs of this file's measurements run warm; that does not invalidate the ratios, but a
# comparison of our cold translation against Metal's warm compile is not one of them.
# WHICH LEG IS WARM IN A STORED RECORDING, since the file should say rather than leave a reader to
# work it out. METAL'S IS WARM BY CONSTRUCTION AND PERMANENTLY SO: a case's Metal functions come
# from source that does not change, and this machine has compiled them thousands of times, so no
# stored recording on it has ever held a cold Metal compile. OURS IS WARM TOO, but only until the
# translation's output changes: our SPIR-V reaches the same cache as MoltenVK's MSL and then its
# AIR, so a build whose SPIR-V the machine has seen reads warm, and the FIRST run after a
# `SEMANTICS_VERSION` bump -- which is precisely the version that marks the output changing --
# reads cold where Metal still reads warm. So a recording taken once a build has run here is
# warm against warm and sound; one taken immediately after a semantics bump is cold against warm
# and is not. That follows from the measured cache (AIR-keyed, cross-process) and from
# `SEMANTICS_VERSION`'s meaning; it has not been measured as a pair of recordings, and a reader
# who needs it measured should say so rather than assume either way.
# What that closes and what it leaves. It closes the driver: a sibling probe's reading that
# MoltenVK's `pipelineCompile` runs 32 times over 32 blend states in every cache arrangement
# (`probes/pipeline_cache_across_blend_states.c`) is right about the floor as well as the count,
# because Metal charges 32 fragment recompiles for them itself -- blending reaches an Apple GPU's
# fragment epilogue, so a blend state is part of the fragment program. Over 32 siblings the driver
# converts and compiles once for the family (`spirvToMSL` 2, `mslCompile` 3,
# `functionSpecialization` 0, `shaderLibraryFromCache` 62, `pipelineCompile` 32), so there is
# nothing there left to reuse. It leaves our own per-pipeline work with a module already in hand,
# which the `render_pipeline` row's last section names and which is where the remaining narrowing
# sits.
# So the cost this round was sent to find is REAL and it is none of the ten calls it named: it is
# the per-pipeline translation, it is visible only on the cases that create many pipelines, and at
# 3.62x worst it is under the per-case margin of 10x, so the suite's per-case verdict reads
# `within` on every one of them. Neither half of this instrument sees it today. A per-call row
# cannot carry it, and nothing below should be mistaken for it.
# WHAT STILL DESERVES A ROW, then. The per-call gate is right to exist -- replace_region WAS 265x
# with 92% of ours blocked, the caller waiting 1.1 ms where Metal writes through in 4 us, while its
# case total was 0.23x, so NOTHING BUT a per-call gate could ever have seen it. What distinguished
# it is not the size of the ratio: it is that the cost was work Metal does not do at all (a wait),
# rather than work Metal already did earlier in the case. So before writing a row, answer which of
# the two it is, and put the per-case figure in the row either way. That row is retired at the
# bottom of this header, and the gate having found a bug nothing else could see is the reason the
# file keeps the argument after losing the row.
# A ratio here is a measurement and it moves MORE THAN EITHER OF ITS HALVES, because the two halves
# move independently. THREE independent whole-set passes have now been recorded on this M3 Max, and
# every figure below is from their stored per-case records (`times --write` keeps both legs in each
# case's recording, so a pass can be re-read without re-running it). They are not equal in quality:
#   pass    instrument (metal/ours)   load (metal/ours)   paired cases
# The 07:44 pass is the degraded one, and the instrument says so: it cost 0.275 us a call against
# 0.236 us in the quietest pass, and its figures are not reproducible by the binary that produced
# them -- re-run over the same fifteen cases, that binary reads function_facts at 46.3x and 40.9x
# against the 89.5x it recorded, and its per-case figures agree with the later passes' to within 5%.
# The cause is the CPU the measurement ran on, not the call: one binary and one case set inside one
# minute read 38.8x at the ordinary scheduling class and 75.5x under a background one, while the
# one-minute load average held at 6.1.
# WHAT THE THIRD PASS CHANGES. The movement this file's band was set from is almost entirely that
# one pass. Over the paired rows common to each pair:
# and restricted to the rows both passes resolve above the instrument (RESOLVES_AT), 1.87x / 6.92x,
# 1.58x / 4.96x, and 1.10x / 1.51x / worst 1.97x. The first line is the pair this file's band was
# set from, and reading it back out of the stored recordings reproduces its published figures to
# the digit, which is what says the other two lines are measured the same way. (The three passes
# ran over 1031, 1084 and 1099 cases as the suite grew, so a pair's rows are its common ones; the
# 98-row comparison the band was set from has the same property, and 15 cases of 1084 is 1.4%.)
# BETWEEN TWO UNDEGRADED PASSES THE WORST MOVEMENT OVER ALL 100 ROWS IS 2.00x -- below even the
# 2.43x the original margin / 2.5 divisor was set from. So the ratio is not inherently unstable;
# and `band` being margin / 7.0 rather than margin / 2.5 is paying for a pass the gate did not
# refuse: 0.275 against 0.236 us is 1.17x, under the 1.5x CALIBRATION_MAY_MOVE allows, so the
# calibration reference check passed a pass whose figures move 64x. IT REFUSES IT NOW, and not on
# the instrument's reading of itself -- every quantity the gate already read ranks that pass as the
# best of the three, because a uniformly slow CPU is a steady one. What catches it is the floor
# under the measurement (FLOOR_MAY_REACH): the suite makes hundreds of calls that do almost
# nothing, so both undegraded passes read a cheapest figure of 41 ns on each leg -- one clock tick,
# 0.17 instrument costs -- while this one has none of Metal's 2,979 figures under even the resolve
# line and a floor of 5.15. constant_data_offset, a getter that does nothing, cost 41 ns on Metal's
# leg in both good passes and 3.000 us in that one. So the divisor is now the owner's to lower, on
# the figure that matters: a resolved ratio moves 1.97x at worst between undegraded passes, so 2.5
# puts the band at 4.0x and retires a fixed row there instead of at 1.43x.
# WHAT THAT MEANS FOR A ROW, CORRECTED. This header used to say that six calls "read far over the
# margin in one of those two passes and far under it in the other", and name
# texture_accesses, function_facts, function_facts_from_descriptor, mesh_pipeline_bindings,
# compute_pipeline_with_stage_input and compute_pipeline_bindings. THAT WAS WRONG, and it is why
# nobody localised them: of those six, only compute_pipeline_bindings actually crossed the margin
# (7.5x then 21.7x and 23.6x -- and the pass that read it UNDER the margin is the degraded one).
# 40.6x, 28.5x, 18.5x and 22.6x are not "far under" an order of magnitude; they are over it, in both
# undegraded passes. The sentence confused a ratio MOVING a lot with a ratio CHANGING SIDES, and on
# that confusion four live per-call costs went unwritten. The calls the degraded pass really did
# invent, each over the margin at 07:44 and comfortably within the band in both undegraded passes,
# are these, and none of them has or needs a row: argument_encoder 36.4x then 4.1x and 3.9x,
# copy_rate_map_parameters 29.9x then 0.5x and 0.5x (we are twice as fast as Metal), dispatch 17.9x
# then 4.4x and 4.0x, compute_pipeline 14.8x then 4.3x and 4.7x, and compute_pipeline_for_commands
# 27.2x then 5.1x and 5.5x.
# WHAT BECAME OF THE FOUR, and the per-case check above is what decided it. mesh_pipeline_bindings
# (0.43x a case), compute_pipeline_bindings (0.15x) and compute_pipeline_with_stage_input's
# attribute-stride half (0.07x) are the compile's placement and not a cost: they keep rows only
# because the gate is per call, and each row says so in its first words. The one family whose case
# total goes the wrong way is attribute-format-*, 1.92x and 2.68x on attribute-format-fetches, and
# that is the single genuine per-case cost this whole cluster contains. function_facts and function_facts_from_descriptor have rows too, and
# they also have a FIX, because their cause was structural rather than a timing: both answer
# through the suite's own
# our_function_facts, which reads five MTLFunction property getters, and every one of the five
# recomputed the function's properties from scratch -- a full AIR decode each, for a module-sourced
# function -- so one reflection call decoded one function's AIR five times over, six with the
# constants dictionary, and ten for a specialized function, which decodes again to specialize. The
# stored pass says so without a timing: the one case of the family whose function needs no decode,
# function-facts-visible, is the one case we are FASTER than Metal on (0.2x) while its fourteen
# siblings run 19.0x to 101.6x, every microsecond of it the caller's own CPU with nothing blocked.
# The runtime now memoizes a function's properties as Metal's MTLFunction already holds them
# (metal2vulkan-runtime/src/library.rs), and the redundancy is held by a count rather than a time
# (metal2vulkan-runtime tests::derived_once: reading the getters derives the properties
# once; with the memo bypassed the same test reads ten). BOTH KEEP A ROW BELOW ANYWAY, with the
# figure the stored pass read, because the gate is per call and an unlisted over-margin row fails
# the run. NO ROW HERE QUOTES AN EXPECTED RATIO. What the memo is proven by is the count, which is
# deterministic and needed no quiet host; the ratio was never the cost, as the per-case figures
# say, and an expectation in place of a measurement is the thing this file keeps having to correct.
# Whoever re-measures replaces the per-call figure with what they read and leaves the per-case
# line, which is the half that decides whether anything is wrong.
# texture_accesses is a third thing again, and the gate has it right: 19.3x, 102.4x, 158.5x, on five
# calls whose cheaper leg is a fifth of one instrument cost. It is WITHHELD in both undegraded
# passes and was judged only at 07:44, where the degraded CPU inflated the absolute per-call cost
# past the resolve line -- so a degraded pass can also move a row INTO the gate's judgement. A row
# that thin must neither be added nor retired, which is what src/slow_calls.rs does: the
# instrument's own cost is bracketed per leg and checked against what this chip's recordings carry,
# and against the cheapest figure that leg produced, and a row the measurement cannot resolve
# above that instrument is held in neither direction.
# THE COUNTED FORM OF THE GAP ABOVE, which no gate holds. The per-pipeline translation this header
# names is invisible to both halves: at 3.62x worst it is under the per-case margin, and a per-call
# row cannot carry it. In counts it is legible. Measured on this M3 Max over all 1103 cases, 8 runs
# of the whole selection at a one-minute load of 5.35, in the 539 cases that create a Metal pipeline
# state and carry a cost record:
#   Metal pipeline states created                       1,560
#   VkPipelines we made                                 2,634   = 1.69 each
#   of those, made at a state's creation                1,259
#     taken by a command                                  789
#     taken by none                                       470   = 37% of them
# So 1.69 VkPipelines per Metal pipeline state, 0.30 of them per state made for a command that never
# came. `variant_pipelines_made` is gated per case as an upper bound and `creation_pipelines_drawn`
# from below, and a change that makes one more pipeline per state while the case grows a state used
# to pass both: the absolute counts rise for two reasons at once and an absolute bound cannot tell
# them apart.
# THAT GATE NOW EXISTS, as a count and with no timing window, which is why it is judgeable on a
# loaded host. `cost::PipelinesPerState` is a per-case bound in the case's own recording, kept as
# the two counts it is the quotient of and judged by cross-multiplication: the pipelines our leg
# made (`creation_pipelines_made` plus `variant_pipelines_made`) over the Metal pipeline states the
# case created. The denominator is the suite's own, because the runtime has no count of the states a
# case asks for -- that is a thing the CASE does, through the vocabulary, identically on both legs;
# `states::making_a_state` is the one door every creation on our leg goes through and a source guard
# fails any creation that does not. A case that grows a state reads the same ratio and needs no
# re-bless; a tree that makes more pipelines for the same work fails. A re-bless of that field means
# one thing, and `cost.rs` says so where the field is declared.
# TWO MORE COUNTS NOW HELD, over the committed recordings and so without a device at all: the
# suite-wide ceiling on predicted pipelines no command took (589 rows carry one, 1,446 made, 815
# taken, 631 by none -- a difference is not a defect, since a creation cannot know whether a command
# will come, but a WIDENING one is), and the reach over the 111 of 158 cases whose made ceiling and
# drawn floor together already say they take every one. Both ceilings were re-blessed by the
# whole-set pass named above, and the raise was diffed row by row rather than assumed: all 585
# pre-existing rows read the same made, taken and waste, `taken` did not move from 815, and all
# seven of the rise are four `read-write-tier-*` rows that did not exist and that dispatch rather
# than draw, so no command can take a predicted render pipeline.
# AND THE COVERAGE HOLE THIS CLUSTER KEPT POINTING AT IS CLOSED. 399 of the 1,103 recordings used to
# carry no cost record, among them `vertex-format-constant-step`, `vertex-format-float4` and every
# `blend-sweep-*` -- exactly the many-pipeline sweeps with the worst per-case ratios, so the fix
# that halved their pipeline count was held by nothing on the cases that most needed it. Every
# recording carries one now. The sweeps read 45 made / 45 taken, 45 / 45 and 32 / 32, and
# `integer-vertex-attributes` reads 64 / 64 / 64 where its blessed ceiling had been 64 / 0 / 128:
# the doubled predicted pipeline is gone from the record as well as from the code.
# The largest single share of the 470 is the compute prediction missing because the dispatch names
# its own threadgroup size -- not a defect in the prediction, which a device test now pins as
# serving a dispatchThreads: over the predicted threadgroup (runtime tests::uniform_bind_offsets).
# The suite holds no dispatchThreadgroups: compute case, so the corpus cannot say how often an app
# hits it.
# WHY 1.69 AND NOT THE 2.56 THIS HEADER ONCE IMPLIED, stated so nobody reads a fix as a measurement
# artefact: integer-vertex-attributes reads 64 states, 64 predicted, 64 taken because the point-list
# prediction for an unrasterized state was FIXED (`Predict a point list for an unrasterized render
# state`, with `Census the mispredicted draws and bound the check's reach` beside it). Its earlier
# 64/0/128 was that bug, reproduced over three passes and gated at 128 as the blessed ceiling, not a
# loaded reading. The count fell because the waste went away.
# WHERE THE EXCESS SITS AFTER THE RE-RECORD, over 1,019 rankable rows at loads 3.79-8.61: Metal
# 25.56 s against our 8.64 s, ratio 0.338, with render_pipeline 38.3% of the excess and `wait`
# 28.2%. The two largest single rows are depth16-texel-reads at 160 ms and the extended-swizzles-*
# family at 43-97 ms each, the latter making 71 VkPipelines for 6 compute states with its
# dispatchThreads edge regions charged to `wait`. Both are open.
# So a row here needs a LOCALISED finding, not a pooled ratio: replace_region read 105x pooled and
# 1.2x over the three cases that obviously make it, and 265x over the 16 that actually do.
# WHAT IS STILL OWED is no longer the per-state bound, and the run that paid it says so. Two
# whole-set runs on this M3 Max, `cost --runs 8 --write` and `cost --runs 8 --alone --write`, each
# over all 1,117 cases in one process: 643 recordings carry a `per_state` bound, 2,687 VkPipelines
# over 1,762 Metal pipeline states, 1.525 each, worst row swizzled-storage-rgba8unorm at 11.25. The
# other 474 carry none for a reason the record states -- 464 cases create no Metal pipeline state,
# so the quotient has no denominator, and 10 hold the venue's own refusal. A bound measured over a
# selection still would not do: `judge` refuses any selection but the whole set, which is the shape
# the gate runs in.
# THE ROW THIS FILE WAS STARTED FOR IS RETIRED, and not on a ratio. `replace_region`'s pooled row is
# WITHHELD in every pass that has measured it -- Metal's typical such call costs about a quarter of
# one instrument cost, under the RESOLVES_AT line -- so the pooled figure could never retire it, and
# that withholding is what the header above says protects it. What retires it is the two halves a
# withheld ratio does not touch: the fix it was waiting on, and our own absolute cost.
# The fix landed (`Let a two-plane texture's CPU copies run where every other texture's do`). The
# row said the gap was that we stage a two-plane extended-range upload and wait on it where Metal
# writes through; the call made two internal `vkQueueSubmit`s and waited on a fence for each, and it
# now takes the host-copy path (`VK_EXT_host_image_copy`) every other texture's replaceRegion
# already took. It is proven by a count rather than a time, which is the evidence this file prefers:
# a device test reads 2 host copies, 0 staging submissions and 0 internal submissions.
# And the measurement agrees, in the one quantity that is ours alone and needs no denominator. Over
# the 14 xr-two-plane-samples cases that carried 100% of the finding, one such call each: our own
# cost was 0.83-1.33 ms with 90%+ of it BLOCKED, and is now 5.5-7.0 us with 0.000 us blocked --
# about 180x less, and the wait that WAS the bug is gone rather than smaller. Each case reads
# 1.2-1.4x where it read 125-323x. Pooled over the 494 judged calls our leg went 18,067 us to 711 us
# and its blocked total 16,423 us to 0.
# Stated against this file's own standard, so nobody re-adds the row off a quiet pass: neither
# re-measuring pass was JUDGED, both refused because the host's load moved more than LOAD_MAY_MOVE
# mid-leg (2.75x and 3.19x) with eight other lanes on the machine. The retirement therefore rests on
# the counted fix and on our absolute cost and blocked time, never on the ratio. A pass that reads
# this call waiting again is a regression and wants its row back.
# Fields, tab-separated:
#   call                the Side call
# A COLD MEASUREMENT IS REPORTED AND NEVER JUDGED, so no row here is measured with
# `--cold-shaders`. That switch gives every case a fresh device as well as a fresh shader cache,
# and only on our leg, so a cold reading over the margin does not say whether the cost is our
# compile or first use on a new device: measured on this M3 Max, `target` is 0.9x warm and 14.3x
# cold and compiles nothing at all. Nine calls were over the margin cold against four warm, and
# seven of the nine were one mechanism. src/slow_calls.rs refuses to judge a cold run.
#   measured            the ratio its measurement read, with an x
#   where the cost is   the family it is in, and what the figure splits into
#   waiting on          what Metal does, what we do instead, and where the fix belongs
function_facts
column3: PER CASE WE ARE 25x FASTER: 0.04x over the 15 cases, Metal 343 ms against our 13 ms, because Metal compiles their AIR at `library` (21-24 ms a case) where we spend 0.05-0.25 ms. This row exists because the gate is per call, NOT because the call costs us anything against Metal. 15 calls over 15 cases, one each, Metal 216 us against our 10430 us, EVERY microsecond of ours our own CPU and nothing blocked. LOCALISED to the AIR decode: 14 of the 15 cases run 19.0x to 101.6x, and the one that does not is function-facts-visible at 0.2x -- a library's visible function, whose properties are a constant and need no decode. It is the only case of the family we are faster than Metal on. 40.6x in the other undegraded pass; the 89.5x on record elsewhere is the degraded pass and is not reproducible RE-MEASURED after the memo fix landed, over the whole set in release on this M3 Max, 8 rounds: 8.9x against the 48.4x this row used to quote, our leg 10,429.8 us to 2,840.9 us over the same 15 call(s). The pass was NOT judged -- the host's load moved 3.19x mid-leg with eight other lanes on it -- so the figure is what was read and not a verdict; what stands behind the fix is still the count (tests::derived_once), and our own absolute cost falling needs no denominator.
column4: The suite's our_function_facts reads five MTLFunction property getters, and each recomputed the function's properties from scratch -- a full AIR decode, for the module-sourced functions newLibraryWithAIR makes -- so one call decoded one function's AIR five times, six with the constants dictionary, and ten for a specialized function, which decodes again to specialize. Metal answers every getter from the MTLFunction it already made. FIXED in metal2vulkan-runtime/src/library.rs, which now memoizes the properties on the function object as Metal holds them, and held by a count rather than a time (tests::derived_once, a table of getters each held to one derivation; with the memos bypassed its five rows read 10, 10, 2, 2 and 2). The constants dictionary named above is now memoized too, and the library's reflectionForFunctionWithName: with it. What the fix is proven by is the count, not a ratio: reading the getters computes the properties once where it computed them ten times, which is deterministic and needed no quiet host. The RATIO has not been re-measured and this row deliberately quotes no expectation for it, because the per-case figure above says the ratio was never a cost in the first place. Whoever re-measures should replace the 48.4x with what they read and leave the per-case line, which is the half that decides whether anything is wrong

column3: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-26 AND THE ROW'S OLD THESIS NO LONGER HOLDS ON ITS OWN EVIDENCE. It used to read that this is the one row carrying the cluster's real cost, because its two worst cases were 3.62x and 3.08x and two blend sweeps ran the wrong way. At this tip the two worst cases are 2.2x and 1.6x and BOTH blend sweeps run the right way (write-masks 0.8x, operations 0.6x), 7 cases are within 10x and 0 over it. It is still the dearest pipeline row per call and its per-case figures still go the wrong way on the vertex families, which is why it stays and stays first; it is no longer a row whose cases are 3x. The figures below marked ORIGINAL are the shape the row was written from and are kept only where the mechanism they establish still stands. ORIGINAL, integer-vertex-attributes at 3.62x a case: Metal 37.8 ms (library 23.5, render 7.6, 64 render_pipeline calls 1.7) against our 136.8 ms (64 render_pipeline calls 87.3, render 15.9, library 0.2, elsewhere 33.7), so render_pipeline is 85.6 ms of our 99 ms excess and 85.6 of our 103.1 ms in calls is our OWN CPU, not waiting. vertex-format-constant-step was 3.08x with the same shape (render_pipeline 71.2 ms of the excess). AT THIS TIP, `times --runs 8` over the 8 cases that make the call, 7 done by both legs: Metal 306 calls / 7,415 us / 22.166 us each against ours 306 / 123,747 us / 279.833 us each, 16.7x per call, 86.6% our own CPU; per case integer-vertex-attributes 2.2x, vertex-format-constant-step 1.6x, half4 1.4x, float4 1.3x, instance-step 1.3x, half-output-blends-r16f 0.7x (withheld, three notices), blend-sweep-write-masks 0.8x, blend-sweep-operations 0.6x. That run is a READING AND NOT A VERDICT: the host sat at a one-minute load of 12.6-13.5 and the instrument flagged its own floor at 2.09 instrument costs where the gate allows 1.0, so it asks to be re-run where the measuring thread keeps its scheduling class. The 28.5x in column 2 is the committed recordings instead, which are undegraded and a larger sample. PER CASE over the blend sweeps 0.68x in the original pass, two of them then the wrong way (write-masks 1.55x, operations 1.25x) while carrying Metal's 27 ms library handicap; both now run the right way. The committed recordings now hold 966 calls over 232 cases, Metal 47,861 us against our 1,361,843 us (28.5x), where this row's original pass saw 660 calls over 120 cases, Metal 28,606 against our 886,266 of which 831,583 was our own CPU. ATTRIBUTED, by the per-call cost against how many the case makes: Metal's median falls and ours does not. Metal costs a median 122.3 us a call in the 66 cases that make one, 31.0 us in the 11 that make 5 to 15 and 26.1 us in the 6 that make 36 or more -- which is the mix of its three cheap answers and not an amortization. Measured on Metal's own API with no Vulkan in the process (`probes/metal_pipeline_marginal_cost.m`), those three are an identical descriptor, memoised at 5-11 us; a change that reaches only a small stage, 45 us for a vertex format where a blend state over the same pair is 3.1 seconds; and an AIR some earlier process compiled, MTLCompilerService keying its output on the AIR and keeping it across processes, 27 us warm against 4052 us cold. A distinct fragment-side state on a cold machine gets none of them and costs what compiling a new function costs. The header says the rest. Ours costs 1686.0, 1277.5 and 1205.6 us over the same three groups, flat to within 1.4x. The ratio therefore climbs 13.8x, 41.3x, 46.1x with the call count while our own per-call cost barely moves, and on a case that makes ONE render pipeline we are faster than Metal (render-draw-forms-lines 0.4x). THE ROW'S OLD CLOSING ARGUMENT IS REFUTED: it read that compute_pipeline is 0.4x at 26.2 us a call against Metal's 71.8, so this was the render path and not pipeline creation in general. The committed recordings now read compute_pipeline at 9.50x, 465 calls over 274 cases, Metal 65.0 us a call against our 617.5. Render is worse, not uniquely wrong, and the contrast no longer licenses the conclusion. WHAT A WARM RENDER CREATION IS, measured in four shader-cache cells (`src/bin/render-pipeline-split.rs`): 240-285 us of our own CPU against Metal's 22.2 us for an entire creation, 11-13x, with NO translation, NO VkShaderModule, NO linked-use question and NO driver compile in the call (`driver_pipeline_hits` 1, `misses` 0 on every warm call). The driver IS asked -- one VkPipeline per creation, made on the CALLING THREAD because `RenderVariant::make_at_creation` hands its one piece to `pipeline_pool.join_all(.., first_here = true)` and `pool.rs:361-364` runs the first piece there -- so `our own CPU` in this row has never meant `our code`. Cold additions: our translation plus the linked-use questions 75-155 us a creation; a driver compile with MTLCompilerService already holding the AIR ~23 us; the first compile of that MSL ever 55 ms a creation, or 4.2 ms wall against 0.46 ms CPU where the wait is XPC. WHAT IS LEFT THAT IS OURS: shader-cache artifact lookups that find nothing usable, which at 0476a0e211 read ONE a creation and not two -- `0 hit / 32 missed` over 32 creations with `{function,compute_pipeline,render_pipeline}_{hits,misses}` split by kind, so the earlier reading of two misses against one hit (64 over 32, 128 over 64, with a one-byte memo adding a hit and no miss) is SUPERSEDED, and what it proved -- that they are not the stage functions -- still holds. AND THE DIRECTORY IS NOT WHERE THE TIME IS. Counted rather than timed with `WorkCounts::shader_cache_read_nanos` (`tests::render_directory_trips`): a warm sibling made FIVE round trips before 0476a0e211 and makes THREE after -- the two `stat`s `linked_render` asked per stage were a fact of the stage's compile key and the profile, which no pipeline state reaches, so a sweep of 16 siblings asked 32 times and now asks 0, in both windows, with a negative control showing a `false` is still asked every creation. The three that remain are each keyed by the sibling's own descriptor: its linked-use answers, its variant record and its pipeline artifact, and the answers genuinely differ between siblings (`reflection/linked.rs` reads each attachment's format, write mask, blending and the four blend factors, and `depth_format`), so that keying is CORRECT. The whole directory is 13 us of a 287-318 us warm creation on this M3 Max at load 4 (21.5-24.8 us a sibling of read time), about 4-5%: THIS ROW'S EARLIER `96 us of our 140-157` DOES NOT REPRODUCE and is withdrawn, having been phase marks taken before that counter existed. MoltenVK's 144-180 us on the calling thread stands, so the driver is a LARGER share of a warm creation than this row used to say, not a smaller one. They are `Sources::render`'s two `load_render_pipeline` calls (`pipeline/render.rs`'s `RenderVariant::compiled`), which miss BY DESIGN because `pipeline/sources.rs:240-250` stores the artifact only where re-linking it would translate -- so a sweep over one vertex-and-fragment pair RE-LINKS its pipeline from two cached stage functions on every creation, and that link plus the state's construction is the 240-285 us. `ShaderCacheOptions::memory_capacity` does fire here (it caps `PipelineMemo`, `shader_cache/mod.rs:368`, default 256 MiB / 4096 entries; zero is refused at device creation, so one byte turns it off) and is worth one artifact read a creation, under the noise floor. `cache/scan.rs`'s linear scan is NOT on the warm path at all: it runs only on an artifact decode and a warm creation decodes none
column4: The cases that make many are the sweeps, which vary only pipeline state over one vertex-and-fragment pair (blend-sweep-*, vertex-format-*, integer-vertex-attributes; the blend slot sweeps need nothing of the fragment function). Metal compiles the functions once and makes cheap state variants; our per-call cost says we do the per-pipeline work again for each. What it is NOT is the shader compile: the measurement carried our shader cache over between the cases of a round, so the second and later pipelines of a sweep meet a warm cache and still cost about 1200 us each. For integer-vertex-attributes the translation is now fully accounted and NONE of it is redundant, so no cache is missing there: the case is 2 entry points x 16 attribute formats x 2 step functions, and shader_modules_made reads 34 = 2 + 32. Its 32 PerVertex pipelines share 2 modules, because an integer format read into a float attribute is fetched by fixed-function input in its USCALED/SSCALED form and vertex_fetch_projection's fetch_of drops the format for a fixed-function attribute, so the format never reaches the compile key. Its 32 Constant-step pipelines cannot be: Vulkan has no constant vertex input rate, so metal::vertex::fetch_as returns Pulled for that step, a pulled fetch reads bytes and converts in the shader, and the projection then carries the attribute and layout -- so the format IS in the key and each of the 16 needs its own vertex translation. 2 + 32 is the measured 34 exactly, and the step function being free while the format is not is why. The doubled predicted pipeline below was therefore the ONLY redundant work in this case. What this does NOT explain is the blend sweeps, whose cost is the per-pipeline work with a module already in hand -- though the module count never licensed that inference and the row used to rest it on one: it read shader_modules_made 2 over 32 pipelines and pipeline_layouts_made 1, where write-masks' bounds now read shader_modules_made 4, shared 61, layouts 3 and `functions_translated` 29, a counter that did not exist when the row was written (added at 170988e1ae), and a cold cell reads one translation per creation, 32 of 32. Identical SPIR-V is why only a few modules are made, and that is where the remaining narrowing sits. THE NEXT NARROWING, identified and deliberately not built: blend-sweep-write-masks varies only the color write mask over one function pair, and VK_EXT_extended_dynamic_state3's COLOR_WRITE_MASK_EXT is wired but made dynamic only in a pipeline that reads through snapshots (pipeline/graphics.rs, GraphicsState::snapshot_reads), which these states do not, so 32 write-mask values become 32 VkPipelines where one dynamic pipeline would do. It is NOT proposed on this evidence, for a reason the venue gives: these figures come from MoltenVK, where Metal holds the write mask in MTLRenderPipelineState, so a dynamic write mask there buys a pipeline per bind instead of per creation and may cost more. Collapsing 32 makings to 1 is a claim about a driver with real dynamic state 3, and it needs a release-mode measurement on such a driver before anything is built. Recorded here so the next reader starts from the condition and not from the ratio. The contrast with compute_pipeline_bindings sharpens it: there our own cost falls 35x from the first pipeline on a shader to the eighth, so for compute the expensive part is once per shader; here it does not fall at all across 64, so for render it is once per pipeline. Whatever a render pipeline redoes, a compute pipeline keeps. ATTRIBUTED AND HALVED by that counters run. Every creation made a predicted VkPipeline the draw never took and the draw then made a second, so the per-pipeline work was done twice: integer-vertex-attributes read creation_pipelines_made 64, creation_pipelines_drawn 0, variant_pipelines_made 128, and vertex-format-float4 45/0/90. The cause is the creation-time prediction (pipeline/predicted.rs), which guessed a triangle list for an Unspecified topology class; these families discard rasterization and draw points, so the guess missed 100% of the time. Fixed: the counters now read 64/64/64 and 45/45/45, with shader_modules_made (34, 10) and pipeline_layouts_made (2, 2) unmoved, so SPIR-V and layouts were already shared and only the wasted pipeline changed. The deterministic check is the recorded bound and not a new test: variant_pipelines_made is gated at its reading with the case alone (cost.rs MONOTONE), and the committed recording for integer-vertex-attributes now carries creation_pipelines_made 64 against variant_pipelines_made 64, so the doubling is gone from the blessed ceiling as well as from the code. WHAT REMAINS, and why this row keeps its figures: removing one of two pipelines per creation does not touch the flat per-call cost beneath it. Our cost per render pipeline is still flat to within 1.4x across 64 where Metal's falls 4.7x for the reasons above rather than by amortizing; about half of the 87.3 ms was expected to go, and it is now SEEN TO HAVE GONE: integer-vertex-attributes' render_pipeline calls read 27,064 us against the 87,324 recorded here, a 3.2x drop, and write-masks 13,094 against 64,019, a 4.9x drop -- per creation 1,364 to 423 us and 2,000 to 409 us. Read at load 12.6-13.5 with the instrument flagging its floor, so a reading and not a verdict, and part of it is the two removals that landed at ee518a6383 (stage digest derivations 32 to 0 over a 16-sibling sweep, pipeline-artifact encodes 16 to 0) which every recording in this file predates. The old claim that our cost is flat to within 1.4x across 64 while the ratio climbs 13.8x, 41.3x, 46.1x with the call count is gone: the 7 sweep cases now sit in a 14.1-18.6x band. The blend sweeps make rasterizing states, read 32/32/32 before and after, and are NOT this cause; they no longer run the wrong way at all (write-masks 0.8x, operations 0.6x). FOR THE OWNER: the cost half was not blind to this one, which is the lesson of the row -- it counted the second pipeline and recorded it as the bound, so a bound re-blessed from a measurement carries whatever waste the measurement had. The times half saw 3.62x on the case and judged nothing, because its margins are per call. THE CENSUS behind the fix, read offline from the committed recordings' own bounds and so load-independent: the committed bounds now hold 511 cases that record making a predicted pipeline, 162 taking every one, 12 taking some but not all (19 wasted) and 337 recording no take, where the census this fix was built from read 356 cases, 99 taking every one, 206 never drawing and 51 mispredicting a draw they did make, paying 121 pipelines twice. Bounds alone cannot split `no take` into `never draws` and `mispredicted every one`, so the totals have moved and the 206/51 split cannot be restated from them. The 206 are NOT a defect -- a creation cannot know whether a draw will come, and paying the compile there is the point, since Metal pays it at library creation -- so the 121 are the whole of this bug and integer-vertex-attributes is 64 of them. A SECOND and distinct mispredict shape sat in the tail and NO LONGER APPEARS: no sample-positions-* or sample-fills-* row reads a partial take any more, where 34 of the 51 once wasted exactly 1 of 1, and GraphicsKey carries sample_positions and pass, neither of which a creation can know, so those cannot be predicted by a better guess at all; one pipeline a case, no per-case ratio, recorded here rather than fixed. THE CHECK REACHES EVERY CASE: every recording carries a cost record (1,122 when this was written), vertex-format-float4, vertex-format-constant-step and the blend sweeps among them, so the bounds hold for every case this row quotes and not only for integer-vertex-attributes. AGENTS.md gives pipeline-creation time its own ceiling rather than the device API's, so the row records the gap meanwhile

column1: compute_pipeline_bindings
column3: PER CASE WE ARE 6.5x FASTER: 0.15x over the 13 cases, Metal 320 ms against our 49 ms, every case between 0.01x and 0.32x, because Metal compiles their AIR at `library` (22-27 ms each) and we translate it here (1.0-6.9 ms). There is no cost gap to attribute. 13 calls over 13 cases, ONE call each, Metal 1755 us against our 41471 us, of which 40054 us is our own CPU: Metal a median 136.5 us a call against our 3004.8 us. The family has 15 cases and all 15 record the call on both legs; 12 are over the margin, 12.4x to 43.3x, and three are under it -- function-bindings-argument-buffer 0.3x, function-bindings-data-types-tables 1.5x and function-bindings-visible-function-table 1.7x. The sums above are that pass's 13. LOCALISED, by the one control the suite already contains: compute_pipeline_reflection_under makes the SAME runtime call (new_compute_pipeline_state_with_function_and_reflection) over the same three shader families and reads 0.7x -- because its cases make EIGHT each where these make one. On texture-slots, ours costs 1922 us for the one call here and 55 us a call over the eight there, while Metal costs 88 us and 29 us. OUR FIRST PIPELINE ON A SHADER COSTS ABOUT 1900-6900 us AND THE SECOND ONWARDS ABOUT 55 us; Metal's first costs 88-190 us. 21.7x in the other undegraded pass. A LIBRARY'S ENTRIES NOW DECODE ONCE BETWEEN THEM, at ff076cd047. Nothing in a module's decode depends on which entry is compiled, so `StageEntries` -- the object the device's pipeline memo already shares between every creation -- keeps each module's decode by its AIR hash, bounded at 4 decodes and 32 MiB with the least recently used evicted, and a request that shares nothing keeps nothing. Counted (`tests::library_entries_decode_once`): the six entries of `reflection/encoder_types` read 1 decode and copy 5 where they read 6, and a creation's plain question about its stage plus that stage's own compile read 1 where they read 2; work units a sibling entry fall 43,197 to 11,451. Release, M3 Max, load 5.33, median of 60 rounds: a round compiling all six once costs 3,819.6 us against 6,313.0, 39% less, with every entry still specialized and compiled from scratch. THIS ROW'S OWN 13 CASES ARE UNCHANGED BY IT: each uses a different shader and makes exactly one pipeline, so none asks twice, and `translate-split once` reads identical work units and ledger peaks for all 15 fixtures. The floor this row names is still ONE TRANSLATION PER SHADER; what moved is the second entry of a library. Also at that tip: `specialize_one`'s second SHA-256 over the bitcode is gone, reading `FunctionInfo::air_hash`, which was 0.96% of a translation
column4: This is a first-use cost on a shader, not a per-pipeline one, and the 22x is what it looks like undiluted: each function-bindings-* case uses a different shader and makes exactly one pipeline, so each pays the whole of it, while compute_pipeline_reflection_under's cases spread the same cost over eight and it disappears. The 35x our own figure amortizes across those eight says the repeated part is small and the once-per-shader part is large. ATTRIBUTED, and it IS the AIR-to-SPIR-V translation. Driving the same call over the family's own fixtures, in release under m2v_gpu on an M3 Max with a shader-cache directory per fixture, the one translation of the kernel is 66-88% of the cold creation: 1.0-5.3 ms of 1.4-8.8 ms. functions_translated reads 1 with functions_shared 0 on the first creation and 0 with 1 on the second, in every fixture, so the 35x this row inferred from timings is now a count -- one translation a shader and none thereafter, 1.4-8.8 ms against 11-41 us. It is once per shader because the memo key is FunctionCompileKey (AIR hash, entry name, constants, profile fingerprint, canonical lowering inputs, linked functions) in Sources::function. The same run retires two leads this row carried. No VkPipeline is made in this call at all -- creation_pipelines_made 0 and variant_pipelines_made 0, because without requiredThreadsPerThreadgroup the dispatch-making predicts nothing -- so no SPIR-V-to-MSL and no Metal compile is inside the figure, which is why all of it is our own CPU. And the binding reflection is not where to look: it costs 0.7-3.9 us off the compiled stage, where deriving it from AIR would cost 82-604 us, and this path never does that. The richness of the reflected arguments does not survive either: tables_in_arguments and textures translate in 1.16 and 1.01 ms while this row's per-call figures put them 21x apart. ONE TRANSLATION PER SHADER IS THE FLOOR, and moving it to library is refused -- we translate only the entry a pipeline asks for, which is why our library costs 0.09-0.78 ms against Metal's 22-27 ms, and reflection/encoder_types is the proof: six entries over 157 KB of AIR, one per case, so an eager library translation would make each of those cases pay all six. AGENTS.md's only numeric ceiling is 20 seconds and 500 MiB per translation attempt, and 6.9 ms is 0.03% of it, so this row's gap is a per-call ratio and not a bound anything exceeds. THE PER-CALL FIGURES ABOVE SHOULD NOT BE REASONED FROM: the recorded 144 us for data-types-tables, 36 us for argument-buffer and 157 us for visible-function-table are not reproducible -- a cold measurement of that same fixture reads 1.42 ms -- and neither cache warmth nor case order explains them, since function_bindings is the first family in cases.rs to make a pipeline on any of these shaders

column1: compute_pipeline_with_stage_input
column3: PER CASE THIS IS THE ONE THAT MOVES, and attribute-format-fetches is the case to chase: it is 2.7x (Metal 48.3 ms against our 132.1 ms) while its sibling attribute-format-class-crossings is 0.3x and attribute-stride-* is 0.2x and 0.0x, so the pair is 1.73x and the family total is the only one of the pipeline rows that goes the wrong way. 112 calls over the 7 cases that measure (8 make it; attribute-stride-inline-bytes is unmeasured, a known gap at known-gaps.tsv line 83), Metal 4082 us against our 23147 us; 5.8x in a second pass of the same selection. THE CALL IS OURS AND IT IS 9% OF THE CASE. No VkPipeline is made inside the call at all: variant_pipelines_made, driver_pipeline_hits and driver_pipeline_misses read 0 on every one of fetches' 29 calls in three cache cells and two runs (src/bin/stage-input-split.rs), because the creation predicts a region's pipeline only where the descriptor states requiredThreadsPerThreadgroup (pipeline/dispatch_making.rs). The cells split the 394 us call 62% our AIR-to-SPIR-V translation / 38% the rest of it with a module in hand, and the cold cell's 394 us equals the suite's own 404 us, which says the suite measures our cold translation every round -- run.rs::open gives each round a fresh ScratchCache while MTLCompilerService is cross-process and permanently warm. THE CASE IS THE DRIVER'S, off the calling thread: of fetches' 83.8 ms excess, 63.5 ms is elsewhere against Metal's, 11.4 ms is in-call CPU (29 x 244 us translation + 29 x 149 us warm path) and 11.5 ms is more blocked at wait. attribute-format-class-crossings makes 16 such calls and never dispatches, so its elsewhere is 0.265 ms a row against fetches' 2.367: about 2.10 ms a row arrives with the dispatch, where the counters put 29 pooled VkPipeline makings -- 61 of the 63.5 ms, an upper bound since the cache writer runs there too. WHAT IS LEFT THAT IS OURS: a warm creation that translates nothing and asks the driver for nothing still costs 149-190 us against Metal's 38.5 for the whole creation, which is 4.3 ms of the 83.8 and is unexplained. STALE AND CORRECTED: 19.9x over 37152 us and 48 calls, the family figure 1.92x (an average of a case 3x FASTER than Metal with one 2.7x slower, which is why a family figure is not a finding here), "all of it our own CPU", 936.1 us on attribute-stride-buffer's one call (now 370.0) and "a ONE-call case costs us more per call than the 29-call case" (now inverted, 370.0 against 404.0). Metal's own one-call figure moved 83.4 to 130.7 us. Measured over an 8-case selection, 8 rounds, twice, one-minute load 6.9 and 6.1, instrument 0.238-0.244 us; NOT a whole-set pass
column4: Our cost rises with the siblings in the two format sweeps only, and the probe in the previous column refutes that as the mechanism: what rises is the module translation, not the pipeline and not the sibling count, and a call that is cheaper than Metal's alone cannot be explained by pipeline creation being expensive. The two cases that make many are attribute-format sweeps over one kernel (attribute-format-fetches, attribute-format-class-crossings), so what varies between siblings is the stage-input descriptor alone. ANSWERED, and it is not the stride: measured on an M3 Max via MoltenVK, driving the cases' own descriptors through the runtime, attribute-format-fetches' 29 rows carry 29 distinct attribute-format tuples over ONE constant stride and make 29 shader modules with none shared -- one per row, irreducible, because the format is the decode -- while attribute-stride-* uses MTLBufferLayoutStrideDynamic, already the pushed form, and makes 1 module over 29 creations. Pool::has_room is ruled out too: the device's kept pools hold 3 blocks and 3 free ranges that never move over 400 creations. Nothing in WorkCounts rises over 410 creations and per-creation cost is flat across eight groups of 50. What remains is that each of this case's siblings is a cold shader where the one-pipeline cases hit a module the round already made: a cache-warmth difference between cases, not a structure that grows with the siblings. THAT CONTRAST IS NOW INVERTED and the warmth reading with it: the ONE-call attribute-stride-buffer costs 370.0 us a call against the 29-call case's 404.0, so a one-call case no longer costs more per call -- it reads a process warm-up rather than a cold shader, the first call of a process costing 1.0-13.7 ms while the first call on a shader in steady state costs 394 us

column1: mesh_pipeline_bindings
column3: PER CASE WE ARE 2.3x FASTER: 0.43x over the 2 cases, Metal 45.4 ms against our 19.4 ms. 16 calls over 2 cases, 8 each, Metal 962 us against our 19070 us, all of it our own CPU: 60.2 us a call against our 1191.9 us. Both cases are over the margin, 20.3x and 19.2x. 18.5x in the other undegraded pass
column4: Mesh pipeline creation with reflection, for an object-and-mesh stage pair. THE COUNTERS HALF IS BLIND TO THIS COST, which is the finding and the reason the row is not attributed. The case makes 8 states from ONE descriptor, varying only MTLPipelineOption -- the same shape as pipeline-options-texture-slots, where the 8 compute states cost 4 us each after the first and the counters read creation_pipelines_made 1, variant_pipelines_made 1, shader_modules_made 1. Here all 8 cost about 1390 us (median 1341 against a per-call mean of 1392, so none of them is a first-use outlier) and `cost --show` moves only 16 of the runtime's 471 counts, 4 of them in the translation region: shader_modules_made 4 with 28 shared and pipeline_layouts_made 1 with 7 shared, so modules and layouts ARE reused, and creation_pipelines_made and variant_pipelines_made do not move at all although their doc covers a render state's predicted key. ATTRIBUTED, and this row's own elimination of reflection was the error that hid it. The claim here was that reflection is cached on the PipelineKey and not the options, so the 8 states should share a key: true of the render path and false of the mesh path, which never built a key at all. The 8 shared nothing. Each state, and each read of a getter, did a full AIR decode of the object, mesh and fragment stages, reaching neither the shader cache nor any memo, while the drawing path went through the cache under render_descriptor_key -- so the 11.1 ms of wall that no counter accounted for was those decodes. Mesh reflection is now routed through the cache and memoized, and it is held by a count: tests::mesh_reflection_derived holds 2 states and 4 getter reads to 1 derivation, reads 0 with the routing removed, and a companion requires two different descriptors to derive 2 so the key cannot be too coarse. So the per-creation counter this row asked for is NOT owed: the cost is attributed and a derivation count holds it. The lesson the row keeps is that eliminating a cause by reading the path that caches it, rather than the path the case takes, eliminated the actual cause

column1: render_pipeline_with_reflection
column3: PER CASE WE ARE 12.5x FASTER: 0.080x over the one case that makes it, Metal 28.4 ms against our 2.3 ms, because Metal compiles the AIR at `library` (28.1 ms, 27.3 of it blocked) where we spend 0.26 ms. This row exists because the gate is per call, NOT because the call costs us anything against Metal. One call over one case (render-state-texture-accesses), Metal 213.0 us against our 1128.1 us = 5.30x; 4.35x (198.3 against 862.9) in the other undegraded pass, and 0.060x a case there. ONLY 61% OF OURS IS OUR OWN CPU: 690.6 us ours against 437.5 us BLOCKED, the only blocked half among this file's pipeline rows. The counters put one VkPipeline and two VkShaderModules inside the call (creation_pipelines_made 1, variant_pipelines_made 1, shader_modules_made 2), so the wait is the driver's Metal compile -- read off the counts, not measured -- and the case never draws (no cmd_bind_pipeline), so it is one of the never-drawing creations render_pipeline's census declares not a defect. NOT A PROCESS WARM-UP: both legs run their 8 rounds in one process and the figure is the median of the rounds' medians, and the round medians span 790-1865 us at 19:57 and 835-925 us at 16:06, never the 1.0-13.7 ms a process's first creation costs. STALE AND CORRECTED: the 14.7x this row quoted, 291 us against 4274 us with 3946 us of it our own CPU, is reproducible from NO stored recording in this tree; the three stored whole-set passes read 7.19x (degraded 07:44), 4.35x and 5.30x, so this call has been UNDER the 10x margin in every stored pass and the row is in the band, not Known
column4: The same pipeline-creation path as render_pipeline plus reflection; listed separately because one call is too thin a measurement to fold into that row

column1: tile_pipeline
column3: PER CASE WE ARE 31x FASTER: 0.032x over the one case the gate judges, Metal 22.3 ms against our 0.715 ms, because Metal compiles the AIR at `library` (22.2 ms, 21.6 of it blocked) where we spend 0.12 ms; 0.290x over all 8 cases that make the call (Metal 250.8 ms against our 72.7 ms), 0.284x in the other undegraded pass.
